class_guess: Bell eats counter, two bells: the IndBECv1 _3ary table (decider-proved from start B) run from start A
summary: Same table as a decider-proved machine; from start A it runs two bells into a wide-digit ternary counter
mechanism: Bell + counter: a 00 marker in a field of 101 blocks moves one block right per pass (F); each pass first adds 1 to a base-3 counter on the right (K1-K6 = the cert's side_3ary rule, mirrored).
Counter digits can be wide: d (110)^n 0 with d = 000/110/010 for 0/1/2 (n = 0 gives 0000/1100/0100); rules I0, I2, I1a, I1b. A digit right after a wide 2 uses 0011/1111/0111 (J0, J1).

From A the tape holds two big bells that take turns (the idle one is a wide digit), one small wide digit and 4-cell digits, up to 5e9; start B has one bell. Bell hand-over (E) and the carry past J2 are not pinned. Only halt: A> 0 1 0; none in 1e10 steps.

template.diff: same table: mirror + rename (ours A,B,C,D,E,F = cert F,A,B,C,D,E); the cert starts in our B, we start in A (our first step writes the one extra 1)
template.note: The cert's rule set = K1-K6 (side_3ary_Pos_inc_rule, QL = QR = our C) + one bell found by the hlin decider (config_T_bsz 745 3). Ours adds a second big bell and wide counter digits. Same config on our flipped table: decider false at T = 746, 1000, 2000, 5000, 20000, and with mnc 3 or 4 at T = 5000 (~2 min each); sibling 707 false at T = 745. On the cert: proved in 4.4 s.

strategy: Finish the small decider grid (mnc 3/4, block size 0, sibling 707). If none proves it, write a hand proof: an invariant of two bells + ternary counter whose low digits are idle fields; prove F, K1-K6, I0-I2 and the two missing rules (I1, E) in Rocq, starting from BellEatsCounter_1RB0RF.v (upstream HEAD) or the _3ary config, then flip to our orientation (Flip.v).
risks: Bell hand-over (E) and the carry past a digit after a wide 2 (J2) are seen only in traces; their exact case split is not known.
Field count is only observed bounded (2 big bells + 1 small wide digit up to 5e9); an invariant needs it proved.
Hand proof is a multi-stage job; the cheap decider route has failed on 8 configs so far.

checkpoint_questions.text: Fig 3 vs Fig 4: does ours (start A) look like the certified start B plus a second bell (the vertical streaks), rather than a different mechanism?
checkpoint_questions.note: Yes, although ours has more 'drippiness' on the upper right edge of the triangle and a white streak running from the apex diagonally down and to the right, while the certified one has several black streaks running from the upper right edge diagonally down and to the left. Asked whether 'plus a second bell (the vertical streaks)' means the drippiness or something else. Answer: the white streak is the second bell (the boundary between field 1 and field 2, cell 959 of 1,836 at 1e8, right after field 1's 319 blocks of 101); the drippiness is the counter at the right end, whose digits have mixed widths and sometimes run as small nested bells.

checkpoint_questions.text: Close-up: do you see short bounces between two nearby columns (one bell step each) and occasional trips to the right end (counter visits)?
Should we spend one more stage on decider configs (cheap, ~2 min per try) before building the hand proof (multi-stage)?
checkpoint_questions.note: 'sure'. Already superseded: the decider-config stage (decider2) ran on 2026-10-12 before the hand-proof stages; the open call is now decision.json (grammar2 vs park).
